---
title: "Writing a report from evidence"
subtitle: "Choose evidence before generating sentences"
description: "Learn how to write a short report from results with recorded evidence. Keep the source reference for every factual sentence."
categories: [natural language generation, report writing, data to text]
---

Nia finished the next-token study. The archive team wants a short report,
not a folder of CSV files and not a guess about why one model scored better.

**Report writing** is a natural language generation application. A
**data-to-text** workflow selects content with source evidence and orders the claims. It
converts the claims into sentences and compares the result with its sources.
Templates or a language model can produce the sentences. Neither method makes a
claim correct.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn

This lesson shows how to:

- state a report's audience, purpose, and exclusions
- keep one evidence row for each reported value
- separate content selection, document planning, and sentence realization
- generate a deterministic report with `glue`
- reject fluent claims without evidence
- keep factual checks separate from human prose checks.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

options(warn = 2)
stopifnot(identical(getOption("warn"), 2L))
```

## Start with the reporting decision

The audience is the archive team. The team must decide whether the
validation-selected trigram improves on the unigram baseline on the test
speeches. The report need not explain how people write or why one context
length performs best. It also need not predict results for another corpus.

The brief limits the report before sentence generation:

- include the validation choice and untouched-test comparison
- state the tokenizer, corpus, and unknown-token limit
- exclude causes, transfer claims, and claims about factual writing quality.

## Build an evidence ledger

An **evidence ledger** is a table that gives each usable result an ID. Each
report sentence can refer to source records. This approach establishes sources
before writing, rather than adding them afterward.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(glue)

validation_results <- read_csv(
  "data/inaugural/next-token-validation.csv",
  na = c("", "NA"),
  col_types = cols(
    split = col_character(),
    model = col_character(),
    context_tokens = col_integer(),
    interpolation_strength = col_double(),
    next_token_rows = col_integer(),
    oov_target_share = col_double(),
    seen_context_share = col_double(),
    mean_log_loss = col_double(),
    perplexity = col_double(),
    selected = col_logical(),
    selection_reason = col_character()
  )
)
test_results <- read_csv(
  "data/inaugural/next-token-test.csv",
  na = c("", "NA"),
  col_types = cols(
    split = col_character(),
    model = col_character(),
    context_tokens = col_integer(),
    interpolation_strength = col_double(),
    next_token_rows = col_integer(),
    oov_target_share = col_double(),
    seen_context_share = col_double(),
    mean_log_loss = col_double(),
    perplexity = col_double(),
    top_1_accuracy = col_double(),
    role = col_character()
  )
)
test_by_speech <- read_csv(
  "data/inaugural/next-token-test-by-speech.csv",
  na = character(),
  col_types = cols(
    speech_id = col_character(),
    next_token_rows = col_integer(),
    model = col_character(),
    perplexity = col_double()
  )
)

validation_trigram <- validation_results |>
  filter(selected)
test_uniform <- test_results |>
  filter(model == "uniform")
test_unigram <- test_results |>
  filter(model == "unigram")
test_trigram <- test_results |>
  filter(model == "trigram")

perplexity_reduction <- 1 -
  test_trigram$perplexity / test_unigram$perplexity

paired_test <- test_by_speech |>
  select(speech_id, model, perplexity) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = model,
    values_from = perplexity
  ) |>
  summarise(
    test_speeches = n(),
    trigram_wins = sum(trigram < unigram),
    ties = sum(trigram == unigram),
    trigram_losses = sum(trigram > unigram)
  )

evidence_ledger <- tribble(
  ~evidence_id, ~source_artifact, ~split, ~measure, ~value, ~unit, ~limit,
  "E1", "next-token-validation.csv", "validation", "trigram perplexity",
  validation_trigram$perplexity, "perplexity",
  "trigram with interpolation strength 100, minimum across 13 candidates",
  "E2", "next-token-test.csv", "test", "uniform perplexity",
  test_uniform$perplexity, "perplexity",
  "2,500 equally likely vocabulary items",
  "E3", "next-token-test.csv", "test", "unigram perplexity",
  test_unigram$perplexity, "perplexity",
  "predeclared baseline under the same tokens",
  "E4", "next-token-test.csv", "test", "trigram perplexity",
  test_trigram$perplexity, "perplexity",
  "selected on validation speeches",
  "E5", "next-token-test.csv", "test", "trigram top-1 accuracy",
  test_trigram$top_1_accuracy, "share",
  "one highest-probability guess per row",
  "E6", "next-token-test-by-speech.csv", "test", "speech-level wins",
  paired_test$trigram_wins, "speeches",
  "paired against the unigram on the same test speeches",
  "E7", "next-token-test.csv", "test", "targets mapped to `<unk>`",
  test_trigram$oov_target_share, "share",
  "the original unseen token is not recovered",
  "E8", "data-raw/build-next-token-study.R", "study", "token rule",
  NA_real_, "setup",
  "lowercase ASCII alphabetic tokens, training-only vocabulary",
  "E9", "R/inaugural-corpus.R", "study", "corpus grain",
  NA_real_, "setup",
  "reconstructed inaugural paragraphs, paragraph-bounded contexts"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  evidence_ledger |>
    mutate(
      value = case_when(
        unit == "share" ~ sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * value),
        unit == "speeches" ~ as.character(as.integer(value)),
        unit == "setup" ~ "documented",
        TRUE ~ sprintf("%.1f", value)
      )
    ),
  col.names = c(
    "Evidence ID",
    "Source artifact",
    "Split",
    "Measure",
    "Value",
    "Unit",
    "Limit"
  ),
  caption = "Evidence records available to the report",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(evidence_ledger$evidence_id, paste0("E", 1:9)),
  identical(validation_trigram$model, "trigram"),
  identical(validation_trigram$interpolation_strength, 100),
  identical(
    validation_trigram$perplexity,
    min(validation_results$perplexity)
  ),
  identical(round(validation_trigram$perplexity, 1), 133.3),
  identical(round(test_uniform$perplexity, 1), 2500.0),
  identical(round(test_unigram$perplexity, 1), 240.7),
  identical(round(test_trigram$perplexity, 1), 145.3),
  identical(round(test_trigram$top_1_accuracy, 3), 0.192),
  identical(paired_test$test_speeches, 13L),
  identical(paired_test$trigram_wins, 13L),
  identical(round(perplexity_reduction, 3), 0.396),
  identical(round(test_trigram$oov_target_share, 3), 0.117),
  identical(
    evidence_ledger$source_artifact[8:9],
    c("data-raw/build-next-token-study.R", "R/inaugural-corpus.R")
  ),
  all(is.na(evidence_ledger$value[8:9]))
)
```

The records contain more than numbers. Each records the split, measure, unit, and
limit. E1 contains no final test results. E2 through E4 are comparable
because they use the same test rows, tokenizer, and vocabulary.

## Decide which claims belong

**Content determination** chooses the facts the report will include. A fluent
sentence can still fail here.

```{r}
candidate_claims <- tribble(
  ~claim_id, ~claim, ~evidence_ids, ~status, ~reason,
  "C1",
  glue(
    "The trigram with interpolation strength 100 had the lowest ",
    "validation perplexity ({round(validation_trigram$perplexity, 1)})."
  ),
  "E1",
  "supported",
  "describes the recorded selection result",
  "C2",
  glue(
    "On test speeches, trigram perplexity was ",
    "{round(test_trigram$perplexity, 1)} versus ",
    "{round(test_unigram$perplexity, 1)} for the unigram baseline."
  ),
  "E3;E4",
  "supported",
  "compares the same unit and test rows",
  "C3",
  glue(
    "The trigram's highest-probability token matched ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * test_trigram$top_1_accuracy)} ",
    "of test rows."
  ),
  "E5",
  "supported",
  "reports the decision rule separately from perplexity",
  "C4",
  glue(
    "The trigram reduced test perplexity by ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * perplexity_reduction)} ",
    "relative to the unigram baseline."
  ),
  "E3;E4",
  "supported",
  "derives a comparison from two test perplexities",
  "C5",
  glue(
    "The trigram had lower perplexity in ",
    "{paired_test$trigram_wins} of {paired_test$test_speeches} ",
    "paired test speeches."
  ),
  "E6",
  "supported",
  "uses the paired speech-level comparison",
  "C6",
  paste(
    "The study uses lowercase alphabetic tokens from reconstructed",
    "inaugural paragraphs."
  ),
  "E8;E9",
  "supported",
  "states the token rule and source grain",
  "C7",
  glue(
    "{sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * test_trigram$oov_target_share)} ",
    "of test targets were mapped to an unknown-token bucket."
  ),
  "E7",
  "supported",
  "states the recorded unknown-token limit",
  "U1",
  "The trigram understands presidential language.",
  NA_character_,
  "reject",
  "perplexity does not measure understanding",
  "U2",
  "Using a trigram will improve report writing.",
  NA_character_,
  "reject",
  "the study did not evaluate reports"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  candidate_claims,
  col.names = c("Claim ID", "Candidate sentence", "Evidence IDs", "Decision", "Reason"),
  caption = "The workflow examines candidate claims before document planning",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(
    candidate_claims$status,
    c(rep("supported", 7), "reject", "reject")
  ),
  identical(
    candidate_claims$evidence_ids[1:7],
    c("E1", "E3;E4", "E5", "E3;E4", "E6", "E8;E9", "E7")
  ),
  all(is.na(candidate_claims$evidence_ids[8:9])),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[1]], fixed("133.3")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[2]], fixed("145.3")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[2]], fixed("240.7")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[3]], fixed("19.2%")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[4]], fixed("39.6%")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[5]], fixed("13 of 13")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[6]], fixed("reconstructed")),
  str_detect(candidate_claims$claim[[7]], fixed("11.7%"))
)
```

The rejected sentences sound reasonable. They still exceed the evidence.
Perplexity measures next-token probability under one setup. The study contains
no test of understanding and no written-report outcome.

## Plan the document before writing it

**Document planning** sets the order and purpose of the sentences.
**Realization** turns values with recorded evidence into wording. The plan below starts
with the decision, gives the untouched-test result, and ends with the limit.

```{r}
report_plan <- tribble(
  ~sentence_id, ~role, ~claim_ids, ~evidence_ids,
  "S1", "selection", "C1", "E1",
  "S2", "test comparison", "C2;C4;C5", "E3;E4;E6",
  "S3", "top-choice result", "C3", "E5",
  "S4", "scope and unknown-token limit", "C6;C7", "E7;E8;E9"
)

report_sentences <- report_plan |>
  mutate(
    text = case_when(
      sentence_id == "S1" ~ glue(
        "The study selected a trigram with interpolation strength 100. It had ",
        "the lowest validation perplexity ",
        "({round(validation_trigram$perplexity, 1)})."
      ),
      sentence_id == "S2" ~ glue(
        "On {paired_test$test_speeches} untouched test speeches, ",
        "trigram perplexity was ",
        "{round(test_trigram$perplexity, 1)} versus ",
        "{round(test_unigram$perplexity, 1)} for the unigram baseline. ",
        "This was a reduction of {sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * perplexity_reduction)}. ",
        "The trigram had lower perplexity in {paired_test$trigram_wins} of ",
        "{paired_test$test_speeches} speeches."
      ),
      sentence_id == "S3" ~ glue(
        "The trigram's highest-probability token matched ",
        "{sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * test_trigram$top_1_accuracy)} ",
        "of test rows."
      ),
      sentence_id == "S4" ~ glue(
        "These results describe lowercase alphabetic tokens from reconstructed ",
        "inaugural paragraphs. Vocabulary mapping places {sprintf('%.1f%%', 100 * test_trigram$oov_target_share)} ",
        "of test targets in an unknown-token category."
      )
    )
  )

report_text <- str_c(
  report_sentences$text,
  collapse = "\n\n"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  report_sentences |>
    select(sentence_id, role, claim_ids, evidence_ids, text),
  col.names = c("Report unit", "Role", "Claim IDs", "Evidence IDs", "Generated text"),
  caption = "Every factual report sentence retains its claim and evidence IDs",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

split_id_string <- function(value) {
  value |>
    str_split(";") |>
    unlist(use.names = FALSE) |>
    unique() |>
    sort()
}

used_claim_ids <- split_id_string(report_sentences$claim_ids)
used_evidence_ids <- split_id_string(report_sentences$evidence_ids)
supported_claims <- candidate_claims |>
  filter(status == "supported")

plan_trace_resolves <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(report_plan)),
  function(row) {
    plan_claim_ids <- split_id_string(report_plan$claim_ids[[row]])
    plan_evidence_ids <- split_id_string(
      report_plan$evidence_ids[[row]]
    )
    claim_evidence_ids <- supported_claims |>
      filter(claim_id %in% plan_claim_ids) |>
      pull(evidence_ids) |>
      split_id_string()

    all(plan_claim_ids %in% supported_claims$claim_id) &&
      identical(claim_evidence_ids, plan_evidence_ids)
  },
  logical(1)
)

claim_and_evidence_ids_resolve <-
  setequal(used_claim_ids, supported_claims$claim_id) &&
    all(used_evidence_ids %in% evidence_ledger$evidence_id) &&
    all(plan_trace_resolves)

numbers_match_evidence <- all(c(
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(as.character(round(validation_trigram$perplexity, 1)))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(as.character(round(test_trigram$perplexity, 1)))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(as.character(round(test_unigram$perplexity, 1)))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * perplexity_reduction))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * test_trigram$top_1_accuracy))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * test_trigram$oov_target_share))
  ),
  str_detect(
    report_text,
    fixed(as.character(glue(
      "{paired_test$trigram_wins} of ",
      "{paired_test$test_speeches} speeches"
    )))
  )
))

unsupported_claims_excluded <- all(c(
  !str_detect(
    report_text,
    regex("\\bunderstands?\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)
  ),
  !str_detect(
    report_text,
    regex("\\bcaused?\\b", ignore_case = TRUE)
  ),
  !str_detect(report_text, fixed("improve report writing"))
))

automated_checks <- c(
  "claim and evidence IDs resolve" =
    claim_and_evidence_ids_resolve,
  "numbers match evidence" = numbers_match_evidence,
  "claims without evidence excluded" = unsupported_claims_excluded
)

stopifnot(
  identical(report_sentences$sentence_id, paste0("S", 1:4)),
  identical(length(plan_trace_resolves), 4L),
  all(automated_checks)
)
```

The trace table stays with the report draft. If a value changes, use the claim
or evidence ID to find the corresponding sentence.

## Render the report from evidence

This chunk writes the four planned report units as prose. The generation
is deterministic: the same evidence and templates produce the same text.

```{r}
#| output: asis

cat(
  "### Next-token study report\n\n",
  report_text,
  "\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

expected_report <- str_c(
  paste0(
    "The study selected a trigram with interpolation strength 100. It had the ",
    "lowest validation perplexity (133.3)."
  ),
  paste0(
    "On 13 untouched test speeches, trigram perplexity was 145.3 versus ",
    "240.7 for the unigram baseline. This was a reduction of 39.6%. The trigram had lower ",
    "perplexity in 13 of 13 speeches."
  ),
  paste0(
    "The trigram's highest-probability token matched 19.2% of test rows."
  ),
  paste0(
    "These results describe lowercase alphabetic tokens from reconstructed ",
    "inaugural paragraphs. Vocabulary mapping places 11.7% of test targets in an ",
    "unknown-token category."
  ),
  sep = "\n\n"
)

stopifnot(
  identical(report_text, expected_report)
)
```

## Examine facts and prose separately

The automated checks compare known numbers and IDs with the evidence ledger.
They also search for prohibited claims. They cannot decide whether the report is clear enough for the
archive team or whether that team should act on it.

```{r}
review_status <- tibble(
  review = c(
    names(automated_checks),
    "human factual checks",
    "human prose checks"
  ),
  status = c(
    unname(if_else(automated_checks, "passed", "failed")),
    "pending",
    "pending"
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

knitr::kable(
  review_status,
  col.names = c("Check stage", "Status"),
  caption = "Automated checks do not substitute for human approval",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  identical(
    review_status$review[1:3],
    names(automated_checks)
  ),
  identical(
    review_status$status,
    c("passed", "passed", "passed", "pending", "pending")
  ),
  sum(review_status$status == "passed") == 3L,
  sum(review_status$status == "pending") == 2L
)
```

For a factual check, a reader compares each sentence with the source records.
The reader looks for added causes, populations, or claims that results apply
elsewhere. For a prose check, a reader examines order, clarity, tone, and usefulness
for the named audience. Approval in one check does not establish approval in the other.

## Use a language model for draft wording

A language model can draft alternate wording after the author finalizes the
evidence ledger and report plan. If you use the draft, save the prompt, model,
version, and output. Reject any number, entity, cause, citation, or evidence ID
absent from the ledger. Do the factual and prose checks again.

This lesson does not call a live model. Credentials, model updates, and
random output would make the rendered page hard to reproduce. A plausible
continuation would still not supply evidence for its own claims.

## What to remember

- State the audience and decision before generating prose.
- Select claims with source evidence before arranging sentences.
- Keep evidence IDs, units, splits, and limits with each claim.
- Templates improve reproducibility. They do not establish truth.
- A language model may draft wording, but new claims require evidence.
- Automated factual checks and human prose checks answer different questions.
